title: Runway vs Pika: video controls, editing and plan costs
summary: Compare Runway and Pika as creator workspaces: Gen-4.5, Pika 2.5 keyframes, existing-video edits, commercial plans and the cost of finished clips.
body_markdown:
Choose Runway when your project needs its Gen-4.5 generation controls or Aleph 2 editing workflow. Choose Pika when Pika 2.5 keyframes, task-specific apps or its current model catalog fit the job better. Both now offer more than their own video models. Compare the exact app, output and paid-use requirements before switching; the platform name alone does not determine video quality.


Magic Hour publishes this comparison and offers a competing creation platform. This is a review of current first-party workflows and terms checked November 3, 2026. We did not run a matched output-quality or speed benchmark across Runway and Pika.


## The decision at a glance


Decision


Runway


Pika


New single shot


Gen-4.5 text/image generation; choose exact duration and framing.


Pika 2.5 text/photo generation or another model in Video Studio.


Ordered still sequence


Check the selected model and input mode; Gen-4.5 documentation lists text/image inputs.


Pika 2.5 Frames accepts two to five ordered stills.


Change existing footage


Aleph 2 Edit Studio with a keyframe preview and source limits.


Swap Anything for character, wardrobe, background or prop changes.


Commercial publishing


Runway usage guidance permits commercial use; input rights still apply.


Current paid subscriptions include commercial use; Free does not, even with packs.


Budget comparison


Check plan commitment, selected model, editing and output-format charges.


Check plan commitment and app quote; Create top-ups have separate product boundaries.


## Compare the workspaces, then select the model


Runway versus Pika is no longer simply a contest between two proprietary video generators. Runway documents access to its own and selected third-party models. Pika’s current consumer platform likewise combines its own models with other providers. Buying another subscription may duplicate a model you can already use.


Start with a concrete job: animate a product photo, connect storyboard frames or change the wardrobe in existing footage. Then find the app and selected model that accept your inputs. A platform can host a model while exposing different references, durations, audio options and export settings from another host.


This guide compares the browser creation products. If you are building an application, use our Magic Hour, Runway and Pika API integration guide instead. Developer authentication, job handling and billing are a separate decision.


Sources:[Runway available models](https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/48649877897107-Available-Models-on-Runway) ·[Pika Video Studio](https://create.pika.art/apps/create-video) ·[API integration comparison](https://magichour.ai/blog/ai-video-api-magic-hour-vs-runway-vs-pika)


## For a new shot, compare the actual input controls


Runway’s Gen-4.5 supports text-to-video and image-to-video, with durations from two to ten seconds and 720p output. Its official workflow separates a complete scene description for text-only generation from motion-focused instructions when the source image already supplies the composition. It is a candidate when those controls match the shot you need.


Pika 2.5 offers another concrete choice: a prompt-only five-second shot, a five- or ten-second photo animation, or Frames mode with two to five ordered stills. Its current app documentation specifies a 720p exception for five-keyframe sequences. Pika 2.5 renders are silent; do not confuse that model with audio-capable models elsewhere in Pika.


For a storyboard with a defined beginning, intermediate composition and end, Pika’s ordered-frame route deserves a look. For a single new shot, compare the required duration, framing and movement first. Neither feature list establishes whose output will preserve your particular product label or character.


Sources:[Creating with Gen-4.5](https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/46974685288467-Creating-with-Gen-4-5) ·[Pika 2.5 inputs and Frames](https://create.pika.art/apps/pika-2-5)


## For existing footage, both have editing routes


Runway’s Edit Studio uses Aleph 2.0 to transform existing footage. Its Single edit workflow lets you choose a keyframe, generate the desired image edit and apply that change through the clip. That preview step is useful when a client must approve how a replacement product or wardrobe looks before the full video is processed.


Check the source constraints before moving a project: the guide requires footage longer than two seconds and shorter than thirty, between 480p and 1080p, with no more than ten cuts. It labels Multi-edit and Expand as coming soon. A listed future mode should not be the reason you buy today.


Pika’s Swap Anything app also accepts existing footage, a description and optional reference images for changes to characters, clothing, backgrounds or props. Pika is therefore worth evaluating for footage changes, not only playful effects. Compare the specific change you need with the source performance you must retain; review the finished clip for unintended alterations.


Sources:[Runway Edit Studio workflow and limits](https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/51683104370451-Creating-with-Edit-Studio) ·[Pika Swap Anything](https://create.pika.art/apps/swap-anything)


## Separate free exports from commercial permission


Pika’s current Free plan has no watermark, but it does not include commercial use. Its FAQ explicitly says purchasing a credit pack on Free does not add that permission. Paid Starter, Creator and Fancy subscriptions include a commercial license, subject to the chosen model’s terms and your rights to the uploaded material. Existing legacy subscribers should check their retained plan terms.


Runway’s usage-rights guidance permits commercial use of generated content without a noncommercial restriction from Runway. That does not clear someone else’s likeness, brand, music or source footage. For client work, retain the relevant permissions and the terms applicable to the chosen workflow.


Also inspect the delivery format. Runway documents ProRes and PNG-sequence generation for Gen-4.5 on specified higher plans, with an additional charge. An ordinary downloaded clip, an upscale and a professional intermediate format solve different delivery requirements.


Sources:[Pika commercial use and downloads](https://pika.art/faq) ·[Runway usage rights](https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/18927776141715-Usage-rights) ·[Gen-4.5 output formats](https://help.runwayml.com/hc/en-us/articles/46974685288467-Creating-with-Gen-4-5)


## Price a small project before a large commitment


The current Pika plans are Free, Starter, Creator and Fancy. Its pricing page distinguishes monthly subscription credits from top-ups and says Pika Create packs do not fund the API, iOS app or old.pika.art. Runway also prices access and usage by plan and model. Use the billing interval and actual checkout total, rather than comparing annual monthly equivalents with monthly payments.


For a hypothetical three-shot sequence, plan three candidate generations for each five-second shot: nine attempts, forty-five generated seconds and fifteen seconds you hope to keep. Add sound creation, editing, upscaling and any additional attempts the brief requires. This is planning arithmetic, not an observed acceptance rate.


Record each selected app’s live quote and the remaining balance before producing the batch. Credits from different providers are not the same currency. Divide total spending by the number of clips you would actually deliver, and keep the subscription commitment visible alongside usage.


Sources:[Current Pika plans and credit boundaries](https://pika.art/pricing) ·[Current Runway plans](https://runway.com/pricing)


## When staying is the better choice


Keep Runway if the required edit, export and model are already available there and moving would only recreate a working process. Keep Pika if its Frames or task-specific app meets the brief, your plan permits publication and the current limits are sufficient. You do not need a second subscription merely to access a familiar underlying model.


Consider switching for a specific missing control, delivery requirement or project budget. Save your original media and finished downloads first. Pika’s FAQ also distinguishes the current product from old.pika.art, so check where your existing creations and subscription live before assuming they disappeared.


If the real task is simply animating an existing image, Magic Hour image-to-video is another route to evaluate. Choose its available model and settings for that task rather than expecting it to replace every editor feature. For adjacent platform choices, see Runway versus Higgsfield and Runway versus Kling.


Sources:[Pika account and migration guidance](https://pika.art/faq) ·[Magic Hour image-to-video](https://magichour.ai/products/image-to-video) ·[Runway vs Higgsfield](https://magichour.ai/blog/runway-vs-higgsfield) ·[Runway vs Kling](https://magichour.ai/blog/runway-vs-kling)
